hero.title: Accessibility
hero.subtitle: What we are putting in place — and what we cannot yet put in place — for this first edition of the BAF Camp.
hero.note: This page is expected to evolve as feedback comes in.

intro.title: Why this page?
intro.p1: In this section you will find the accessibility measures that will be implemented, as well as those that will not be implemented during this first edition of BAF Camp. By explaining which measures will be in place during the festival, we hope to allow everyone to make an informed decision about attending and/or bringing the equipment they need with full knowledge of the accessibility of our space.
intro.p2: We are drawing on the work of Les Dévalideuses to build this approach.
intro.definitionText: An accessible space is a space that works to avoid reproducing systemic violence and normalized oppression in our society.
intro.remarksP1: We have chosen to implement only certain measures for practical reasons (lack of time, funding, concrete obstacles encountered on the ground and not anticipated in advance). These shortcomings are not the result of a hierarchy of discriminations nor a political choice. If a future edition of BAF Camp takes place, we will work further on implementing the missing measures while also taking into account the feedback we receive.
intro.remarksP2: We are aware that these measures will not be sufficient for some people to attend, and that this lack constitutes an additional form of exclusionary violence. We are sorry for that.
intro.remarksP3: In addition, the festival programme and organization were mainly built by able-bodied, white, francophone people, which concentrates power among them and means the event will not be fully mixed but will only tend toward inclusivity, which may itself represent another form of "violence".
intro.remarksP4: These measures were notably developed using the Les Dévalideuses accessibility guide.

items.i0: Non-mixed spaces on the festival site (camping, chill space, some workshops).
items.i1: A violence barometer has been established with a qualified person, so the care team can follow a clear protocol in case of violence.
items.i2: A care cell will welcome people who want to rest in a calm and safe space and offer active listening. Active listening can help participants process incidents of violence that may have occurred at the festival and enable the care team to respond according to the wishes of the person who experienced or witnessed the violence.
items.i3: A trained street medics team will be present for medical help.
items.i4: A surveillance system will run 24/7 on the camp (with staff at night) for everyone's physical and emotional safety and comfort.
items.i5: There is no phone line for the care cell during the festival.
items.i6: We cannot guarantee the presence of a trained person for every potential discrimination (queerphobia, ableism, etc.), but we will do everything possible to find suitable solutions.

items.i0Suffix: reflecting the values of BAF Camp has been written and read by all staff, who commit to following it.
items.i1: A briefing at reception will raise awareness among festival-goers about possible discrimination and violence, and the measures planned in response.

items.i0: The staff have received training on violence in festival settings.
items.i1: The care team will brief as many people as possible during setup on issues of classism, LGBTQIA+ violence, dis/ability and VSS.
items.i2: A professional from ASBL Tilt will train staff and volunteers twice on racism in festivals.
items.i3: No training is given by professionals on classism, LGBTQIA+ violence, dis/ability or VSS.

items.i0: Spaces for disabled people will be marked with flowers to avoid stigmatizing signage.
items.i1: The fridge will be accessible to store food for specific diets and medication.
items.i2: Flower-shaped pins will indicate a visible or invisible disability for those who want to use them (their meaning will be explained to everyone).
items.i3: A customizable badge will be available (name/blaze, pronouns, social battery, language, etc.).
items.i4: An SNJ-style tent with around ten camp beds, more comfortable than regular camping, will be accessible on request — limited places, to be booked by email: activismcampbelgium@proton.me.
items.i5: There is no dedicated contact person for the punctual reception of disabled visitors, but a reference person will be available for questions about the measures.

items.i0Suffix: with materials to build games and activities, supported by experienced volunteers for two hours in the morning and two in the afternoon. The space will remain accessible outside these periods without supervision.
items.i1: Activities accessible to children throughout the festival (improvisation, gardening workshops, and more).
items.i2: Changing tables available in or near the washing spaces.
items.i3: The fridge will be accessible for food for babies.

items.i0: Large orientation panels will indicate the different spaces of the festival.
items.i1: Paths and spaces will be sufficiently lit to move around easily.
items.i2: Facilitators will be invited to describe the visual parts of their workshops.
items.i3: There is no dedicated person to greet and orient blind or partially sighted people.
items.i5: Guide dogs are not welcome, following the request of the property owner.

items.i0: More than 60% of workshops will be given in French. Activities in the two large chapiteaux (150p) will be translated into English, Dutch and French. English or Dutch workshops will happen throughout the day.
items.i2: No closed captioning or magnetic loop system.
items.i3: No specific provision for deaf-blind people (tactile sign language, haptic communication).
items.i4: No sign language classes during the camp.

spatial.title: Spatial accessibility
spatial.alertText: There will probably be no access matting on the festival site. The ground is grassy and partly sloped: access to our festival will already be extremely limited for many people with reduced mobility. We are sincerely sorry for this. Accessible areas without slopes are mainly those located along the river (marked in blue on the map). Some workshop areas and the chill zone are located on sloped ground.
spatial.railText: The train journey to Grupont requires at least one change at Rochefort-Jemelle. Since Rochefort-Jemelle station is not independently accessible, assistance for boarding and disembarking must be booked with SNCB at least 24 hours in advance. The route indicated for festival-goers is a forest path. However, we will also provide an alternative access route for people requiring a more accessible surface. Via this route, Grupont station is located approximately 400 meters from the festival grounds. The station does not have an accessibility ramp, and a 3-step staircase must be used when leaving the platform. The road between the station and the festival is paved but lacks sidewalks in certain sections. The first 200 meters are very steep, and the final 100 meters consist of asphalt mixed with gravel.
spatial.terrainText: The festival takes place on grassy terrain. The campsite is reached from the festival by a steep dirt path of 200 meters. The site includes several elevated spaces (slopes ranging from 1 to 3 meters) and areas located on either side of a wooden footbridge. Most other spaces (canteen, bar, main marquees) are on the flat part of the site. The terrain is bordered by a river, which can make the atmosphere very humid and cold at night.

items.i0: PMR parking spaces will be provided near the entrance. However, we cannot guarantee they will remain permanently available: it may be necessary to drop the person as close as possible to the site, then park the car in the village to keep emergency access clear.
items.i1: No guarantee that there will be accessible toilets and washing facilities for PMR users (enough space, handrails, wide door).
items.i2: Risky areas (holes, river) will be marked with tape or signs.
items.i4: PMR needs have been taken into account in the emergency evacuation plans.
items.i5: No dedicated PMR spaces in the different locations. However, on request, we will ensure people can be placed near the stage and we will reserve seats for this purpose.
items.i6: We cannot guarantee a variety of seating everywhere, but we are working on it.
items.i7: No IMO vehicle available from the festival to collect people from the station.

items.i0: An info space will provide a map and programme, and allow questions about organization (time or place changes).
items.i1: Facilitators will be invited to indicate the expected stimulation level (TW, visual effects, violence, shouting), and this information will be available in the programme or at the info point. There will be no strobe lights on festival stages.
items.i2: A chill area without sound and a quiet space in the care zone (as much as possible given the size of the festival). However, due to the festival's relatively small size, noise from stages may still reach the care zone.
items.i3: Noise-reducing headphones will be available in the care area.
items.i4: No accessible sound meter for the different stages.
items.i5: Information will not be made visually or audibly accessible (pictograms, images).
items.i6: Schedule changes will be displayed at the info space, but we cannot guarantee that everyone will be informed via, for example, a festival-wide sound system.

items.i0: Clear signage will indicate the location of different spaces, with maps available at reception.
items.i1: Self-managed tents for activities of your choice, as well as chill and quiet spaces to write or read without interacting.
items.i2: In the large chapiteaux, it will be possible to ask questions in writing or express opinions, transmitted to facilitators, so people can participate without speaking publicly.
items.i3: No writing in FALC (Easy to Read and Understand) for this edition, which makes our communication less accessible. We hope to implement it in a future edition.

items.i0: Masks and gel available in the care space.
items.i1: Hand sanitizer distributed before entering the canteen.
items.i2: The capacity of each space is limited and will be specified on the programme.
items.i3: Wearing a mask will not be mandatory.
items.i4: No requirement to present a negative PCR test to enter the festival.

intro.title: What is pay-what-you-can?
intro.p1: Tickets for the BAF Camp do not have a fixed price. Everyone contributes according to their real means — not just their salary, but their assets, privileges and safety nets. Those who are more financially comfortable pay more to allow those less privileged to attend.
intro.p2: Pay-what-you-can doesn't always work well — people with more means tend to underpay. That's why we invite you to reflect honestly on your situation before choosing your amount.
intro.p3: Of course, every situation is different: if you regularly send money to loved ones or have significant healthcare expenses, take that into account. Our Privilege-o-meter below can help you calculate a price that is fair to your situation.
intro.p4: This festival is a first edition. If we don't cover costs, the project will go into debt and undermine the possibility of future editions. We really count on your generosity and honesty for this project to be a success, especially financially. Any surplus will be redistributed to various (local) struggles via the Fondation Marius Jacob<sup>*</sup> or used to finance next year's edition.
intro.footnote1Text: is a collective, self-managed financial tool that redistributes grants to activists, collectives and social movements in Belgium — and hosts our bank account.

privilegeMeter.title: The Privilege-o-meter — calculate your fair contribution
privilegeMeter.description: Answer the questions below to estimate where you stand economically. This is not a judgement — it's a tool to help you contribute fairly.

plusItems.i0: Your parents own a property in which you grew up.
plusItems.i2: Your parents have the means to help you buy a property.
plusItems.i3: You have received or will receive an inheritance of more than €50,000.
plusItems.i4: You have at least €5,000 in savings.
plusItems.i5: Your parents can support you in case of financial need without it costing them much.
plusItems.i7: You could get a job or professional help through your parents or their network.
plusItems.i8: You go to restaurants, the cinema or cultural activities.
plusItems.i9: You have hobbies such as: music lessons, drawing, hockey, horse riding, tennis, climbing.
plusItems.i10: You have a permanent contract earning more than €1,800 and no dependants.

minusItems.i0: Your parents are afraid of the police / the army.
minusItems.i1: In case of trouble, your parents do not call the police.
minusItems.i2: Your financial support figures had short, precarious contracts / blue-collar jobs.
minusItems.i3: You had to share a room with siblings for financial reasons.
minusItems.i4: Your financial support figure did not finish secondary school.
minusItems.i5: Your grandparents helped with childcare for financial reasons.
minusItems.i7: You have costs related to repression (fines, legal fees,…).
minusItems.i8: You are a student and your parents do not support you (sufficiently).

recoHigh.title: Solidarity rate.
recoHigh.description: You live comfortably: regular leisure, holidays, salary above €1,800 per month, or a prospect of home ownership. You can contribute more for those who cannot.

recoMid.title: Cost price.
recoMid.description: You have a stable income and make ends meet without too much stress. Your salary is around €1,200–1,600 (with no dependants). You might have a bit of savings, or parents to fall back on if truly needed.

recoLow.title: Reduced price.
recoLow.description: You have no assets and no fixed income that gives you a stable daily life. You regularly rely on the solidarity of those around you.

privilegeMeter.formulaNote:
If you score 8 points or more on the Privilege-o-meter → solidarity rate.
Between 4 and 7 points → cost price.
Fewer than 4 points → reduced rate. Feel free to reach out if you're unsure.

hero.title: How to fight together?
hero.subtitle: The program will revolve around this question.

programme.construction: This is a provisional program which could change between now and the start of the festival.

intro.title: Let’s build the program together!
intro.sentence: The camp will explore two concepts:

together.title: Together
together.tagline: Locate ourselves and find our common ground
together.explanation: What do we have in common? How can we improve the inclusiveness of our struggles and make ourselves more accessible? How can we make our disagreements visible and find points of agreement around which we can rally for mutual benefits? How can we emancipate and not oppress each other within our struggles, that is be truly anti-racist, feminist, anti-capitalist and anti-ableist?

struggle.title: Struggling
struggle.explanation: How can we support each other? What subjects are common and what are the places of struggle near us? What strengths and specificities can we mobilise, where and how? What can we learn from our experiences, strategies and tactics? How can we create a powerful, effective and collective logistical network for our struggles?

hero.title: Self-management
hero.subtitle: Some information on how we work

structure.title: Our structure
structure.text: The BAF Camp is a self-managed event. We organise horizontally, with working groups for different aspects (Logistics, Care, Comms, ...) and a coordination working group. Decisions are made by consent and we advocate an anti-authoritarian attitude. The organizing group is made up of people learning together to create these kinds of events, so it is open to anyone. No skills are required.

gt.title: Working groups
gt.intro: Here is the list of the different working groups ("groupes de travails" or GTs in French), send an email by clicking on the button above if you wish to join one of them.

i0.title: GT Care
i0.text: Research and put into practice processes to fight oppressive practices during the organization and the festival itself.

i1.title: GT Communication
i1.text: Manage social networks, website, external communication of the event.

i3.title: GT Logistics
i3.text: Plan the necessary equipment for the festival as well as the logistics of the site (tent locations, setup and dismantling, etc.)

i4.title: GT Programming
i4.text: Propose workshop themes for the festival programme and contact these collectives or people, collect contributions for the programme.

i5.title: GT Money & Legal
i5.text: Define a budget for the festival, contact donors, think about the legal protection of the festival and request the necessary authorizations.

i6.title: GT Coordination
i6.text: Supports other groups and ensures fluid communication between the different GTs.

benevolat.title: Volunteering
benevolat.text1: On site, our goal is for this event to run in as horizontal and self-managed a way as possible. That's why, in order to blur the line between volunteers & “consumers” of the festival as much as possible, ideally, all participants give a bit of their time to help run this festival.
benevolat.stat: We've calculated that if all volunteers work 2 hours a day, the festival should be able to run in a self-managed way.
benevolat.adapt: Furthermore, any task can be adapted if you have a disability of any kind.
benevolat.text2: Feel free to already let us know your volunteering preferences by filling out the registration form. Otherwise, you’ll be able to find tasks to do on the spot in real time! If you have any questions or comments before August 20th, contact us via our email: volunteers@bafcamp.be!
benevolat.text3: The camp will be set up and taken down collectively. We’ll need help! We’ll need to put up marquees and stages, but also create the decor, imagine spaces and build infrastructure out of pallets according to our ideas!
benevolat.text4: But before anything else, don’t forget to get your spot for the event.

kitchen-cleanup.i2: Help pack down the kitchen at the end of the day

waste.i0: Empty the bins across the festival site

waste.i2: Keep the site tidy as you go

hygiene.i0: Clean and restock the toilets and wash areas

hygiene.i2: Empty out the toilet reservoirs (protective sanitary gear provided). You will not be allowed to work a food-related shift for 24 hours

hero.title: Our charter
hero.subtitle: The political and strategic bases of the BAF Camp

pourquoi.title: Why this camp
pourquoi.p1: The BAF Camp is a space to meet, organize and bolster our struggles. It starts from an observation: our rights are declining, repression is increasing and our movements are fragmented.
pourquoi.p2: The objective of the BAF camp is to create links between collectives, share practices and build strong and lasting alliances, while maintaining lively and accessible spaces.

objectifs.title: What we are trying to do

i0.title: Connections
i0.text: Create bridges between struggles and territories (Brussels, Wallonia, Flanders).

i2.title: Get organized
i2.text: Share strategies, debate and find common ground.

positionnement.title: Positioning
positionnement.text: The camp is part of social, anti-fascist, ecological, peasant, feminist, anti-racist, anti-imperialism, decolonial, anti-validist and queer struggles. It is based on an anti-authoritarian approach and seeks to limit relationships of domination, including internally.

items.i0: Refusal of oppression (racism, sexism, validism, classism, LGBTQIA+phobias, etc.)
items.i1: Pay attention to power relations in discussions
items.i2: Those concerned by an issue are put centre stage
items.i3: No emphasis on a particular organization or ideology

fonctionnement.title: Collective operation
fonctionnement.text: The camp is self-managed and based on active participation. It operates through working groups and decisions taken collectively.

items.i0: Horizontal organization based on consensual decision making
items.i1: Everyone participates through volunteer shifts during the camp
items.i2: Openness to new people and groups

cadre.title: Basic framework
cadre.text: The camp is not a guaranteed “safe” space, but a space where we try to build conditions of respect and listening.

items.i0: Respect for others and their experiences
items.i1: Consent (when talking to others, taking photos, physical contact...)
items.i2: Refusal of violent or manipulative behavior
items.i3: Take your share of responsibility in the event of conflict

cadre.note: A team dedicated to care and conflict management will be present during the camp.

accessibilite.title: Accessibility & inclusion
accessibilite.text: Work is being carried out to make the camp accessible to as many people as possible, even if everything cannot be perfect.

items.i0: Interpretation into French, Dutch and English as much as possible
items.i1: Pay attention to specific needs (food, accessibility, etc.)
items.i2: Intentionally diverse spaces (e.g. womxn only activities)
items.i3: Working with relevant groups in the run up to the festival

charteComplete.title: Complete charter
charteComplete.text: This page is a summary. The complete charter details the rules, definitions and processes. Its reading is strongly recommended for participating in the camp.

hero.title: Financing
hero.subtitle: How the BAF Camp is funded and the presentation of our budget in complete transparency.

financements.construction: Site under construction — complete and final information will be announced soon!

sources.title: Funding sources
sources.text: The camp is self-funded. The vast majority of the festival is funded by participants. The majority of financial sources will come from free-price ticket sales, as well as on-site purchases. For that :
sources.cashSubtitle: There are no cash machines close to the site.
sources.subnote: Here’s how we plan to fairly achieve a balanced and sustainable budget:

i0.title: Ticketing
i0.text: Ticket sales represent the festival’s main source of income. The price is pay-what-you-can, with a privilege-o-meter to facilitate conscious and informed free pricing.

i1.title: Bar & Food
i1.text: Revenue from the bar contributes to the events budget. Revenues from food go to the collective(s) running the canteen.

i2.title: Profits?
i2.text: Profits from the event will be used for current or future struggles.

transparence.title: Budget transparency
transparence.text: The festival accounts will be accessible to everyone. The results will be presented after the edition.

items.i1: Reinjection of profits into selected projects
